title: Channel3 vs Shopify Catalog
summary: A single-platform storefront catalog vs. a cross-retailer product data API for AI shopping agents
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Shopify Catalog (the Global Catalog exposed through Shopify’s UCP and MCP endpoints) gives AI agents a clean, deduplicated view of products sold by eligible Shopify merchants. It is free, well structured, and a good choice if every product you want to recommend lives on Shopify.


Channel3 is a cross-retailer product data API: 100M+ products from 25,000+ brands and retailers — Shopify stores included, but also Nike, Nordstrom, Best Buy, Walmart, and the long tail of retailers that run on other platforms — normalized into one schema with prices, availability, retailer links, and affiliate commission built in.


If your agent is a shopping assistant for the Shopify ecosystem, Shopify Catalog is a strong fit. If your agent has to answer “what’s the best commuter backpack under $100?” with results from the whole market — and you want to earn when the user buys — Channel3 is the product discovery backend built for that.


## The core difference: one platform vs. the whole market


Shopify Catalog is a catalog of Shopify. That’s not a knock — Shopify powers millions of storefronts, and the data model is genuinely good: products are clustered under a Universal Product ID, variants carry their own pricing, and each result comes with a direct checkout link. But coverage stops at the platform boundary. Brands that run their own commerce stack, big-box retailers, marketplaces, and department stores simply aren’t in it.


When we ran a “durable commuter backpack under $100” query through it for[our API roundup](https://trychannel3.com/blog/best-product-data-apis-ai-agents-2026) , every result came from a smaller DTC shop. No Nike. No North Face. No Herschel. One result was a demo store on a myshopify.com subdomain; another was priced in Nigerian Naira despite a USD filter. The same query on Channel3 returned Nike, Puma, HP, and The North Face, each with multiple retailer offers attached.


For a product discovery backend, that is the whole question. An agent that can only see one platform will confidently recommend the best option *on that platform* , which is not the same thing as the best option.


## Structured cross-retailer data, without scraping


The obvious way to get beyond a single platform is to scrape retailer sites yourself, or pay a SERP scraper to do it. That trades one problem for another: fragile parsers, inconsistent fields, legal exposure, and a normalization layer you now own forever.


Channel3 sits in between. We ingest product data through direct retailer and affiliate-network relationships and structured feeds, then use multimodal AI to read product pages, match duplicates across merchants, link variants like color and size, and extract attributes. The output is one schema regardless of where the product is sold:


- **Brand as a field.** Shopify Catalog has no structured brand — you infer it from the shop name or parse the title. Channel3 returns` brand` on every product and lets you filter on it.
- **Offers across retailers.** One product, many sellers: “$90 at nike.com, $95 at Foot Locker,” each with its own price, availability, and link.
- **Rich filters.** Brand, category, gender, price range, availability, retailer, color, and other attributes — not just price, shop, and shipping origin.
- **Continuously refreshed prices and stock.** So your agent doesn’t recommend something that sold out last week.


## The affiliate angle


Shopify Catalog is free and it returns checkout links, but there is no commission in the response. If your agent drives a sale, the merchant keeps 100% of it and you have no attribution.


Channel3 is built so the people building shopping agents can earn from them. Every offer comes with a monetizable URL, commission rates are exposed per retailer (up to 3–8.4% on typical apparel and electronics offers), and attribution is handled for you — no affiliate network sign-ups, no per-retailer negotiations. The same API call that finds the product is the one that gets you paid when it sells.


## Where Shopify Catalog is the right call


To be fair to it: if you are building a Shopify app, an agent for a Shopify merchant network, or an assistant that only needs DTC inventory from Shopify stores, Shopify Catalog is free, first-party, and returns native checkout links. Channel3 doesn’t replace that. It’s for the moment your agent has to look past the platform.

## FAQ


**What is Shopify Catalog?**
Shopify Catalog is Shopify’s product discovery layer for AI agents. Its Global Catalog searches products from eligible Shopify merchants, clustered by Universal Product ID, and is exposed through UCP and MCP endpoints so agents can search, look up, and get product details with checkout links.


**Does Shopify Catalog include products from non-Shopify retailers?**
No. Its scope is merchants on the Shopify platform. Brands and retailers that run on other commerce stacks — most big-box retailers, marketplaces, and department stores — are not included.


**How is Channel3 different from Shopify Catalog?**
Channel3 covers 100M+ products across 25,000+ brands and retailers regardless of platform, returns a structured brand field and multi-retailer offers, supports richer filtering, and includes affiliate commission on every offer. Shopify Catalog is free but limited to Shopify merchants and has no monetization layer.


**Can I use Shopify Catalog and Channel3 together?**
Yes. Some teams use Shopify Catalog for native checkout inside a Shopify-centric experience and Channel3 for cross-retailer discovery, comparison, and monetized recommendations.


**How does Channel3 get product data without scraping retailer sites?**
Through direct retailer and affiliate-network relationships and structured feeds, enriched with multimodal AI that matches duplicates across merchants, links variants, and extracts attributes into one normalized schema.


**What does Channel3 cost?**
1,000 free queries to start, then $7 per 1,000 queries. Affiliate commission is included at no extra cost.
